Subject: Invoice 4391 — appearing unpaid in our ledger (need remittance)

Hi Jordan / finance team,

Quick one — our collections report shows Invoice 4391 (period Jun 2026, USD 18,240, VAT inclusive) as past due since 2026-07-02, but when I pull your payments from the bank feed the remittance you sent on 2026-07-05 doesn’t appear to match the invoice reference or VAT breakdown. Our system shows the invoice still open and it’s triggering the next dunning step tomorrow.

Could you please:
- Confirm whether the 2026-07-05 payment (ref: LED-0726-2) was intended for Redwood Inference / legal entity Redwood Inc.
- Share remittance PDF or bank trace (filename, date, amount, reference) for that payment
- Confirm whether VAT was applied net or gross on your side (we’ve seen mismatches before when customers remit net of VAT)

I’ve attached a copy of Invoice_4391_redwood.pdf for reference. If you prefer a quick call to resolve, I’m available today between 1–3pm PT.

Thanks,
Rachel

Hi Rachel — thanks for the note. I pulled our AP records and we did issue a payment on 2026-07-05 for USD 18,240 but it looks like the payment was applied to a different legal entity (LedgerTech Europe) in our ERP. Our bank remittance shows the beneficiary as "Redwood Technologies" — which I can see would not match your invoice reference.

I’ve attached the remittance advice we sent: LedgerTech_remittance_20260810.png. Can you confirm whether we should reallocate this to Redwood Inc. or whether you prefer we issue a fresh payment and reverse the prior one? We can also provide a SWIFT trace if needed.

Also: our AP team noted the VAT line was excluded on our side (we treated it as a reverse-charge for our internal book). If the invoice expects VAT to be collected, that could be why totals don’t reconcile.

Jordan

Subject: LedgerTech — proposed short hold on dunning + exec visibility

Markus / team,

Following Rachel’s notes, LedgerTech (DL-4391) has an outstanding invoice where the customer has evidence of payment but the remittance was applied to the wrong legal entity and VAT was handled differently. Amount outstanding: USD 18,240.

Recommended immediate actions:
- Place a 10-business-day hold on automated dunning for LedgerTech to allow AP to provide SWIFT trace and for us to reconcile (I propose hold window 2026-08-03 to 2026-08-14).
- If AP cannot provide trace by 2026-08-10, escalate to the customer CFO for an immediate resolution (Marissa to draft email).
- If reallocation is not possible and customer issues a new payment, accept and close the open invoice; if the customer claims VAT treatment differs, request a credit note and reissue with the correct VAT profile.

We’ve seen similar cases where an incorrect beneficiary name stalls reconciliation — given the size of the invoice and the strategic nature of LedgerTech (monthly seat usage, potential expansion), I recommend we avoid moving to the next dunning stage while they provide proof.

Action items: Rachel to request SWIFT trace (pending); Markus to confirm hold and approval threshold for any credit notes; Sean to flag collections/CS if conversations go to CFO.

Marissa Cole
Revenue Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Thank you — I agree with the proposed approach.

Decision / guidance:
- Place a dunning hold through 2026-08-14. Do not escalate automated notices.
- If LedgerTech provides a SWIFT trace that proves the payment, collections team to apply payment and close invoice.
- If SWIFT trace is not provided by 2026-08-10, Marissa to escalate to LedgerTech CFO and copy me; if the unresolved amount exceeds USD 50,000, I will engage directly.
- If a credit note is required due to VAT treatment, approve up to USD 25,000 on my behalf; anything higher I need to sign off.

Rachel: please send Jordan a short note confirming hold and requesting the SWIFT trace. Sean: prep the collection timeline in case escalation is required.

-Markus
